nary_nodes.label: Colombia earthquake
evidence: At least 169 people are dead and a state of emergency has been declared after Colombia was hit by one of its largest earthquakes in years.
The magnitude 7.4 quake struck at 07:34 (12:34 GMT) at a depth of 103km (64 miles) in Chocó province, the country's geological service said.

nary_nodes.label: Deaths from earthquake
evidence: At least 169 people are dead and a state of emergency has been declared after Colombia was hit by one of its largest earthquakes in years.
The death toll is likely to rise, with more feared trapped under collapsed buildings.
Many of the deaths have been concentrated in Cali, Colombia's third most populous city.
Cali, located about 200km from the epicentre, was the worst affected with 85 dead.
In Pereira, in Colombia's coffee-growing region, 66 people died.
At least five people also died in Manizales, another city in the coffee-growing region, which is popular with local and foreign tourists.

nary_nodes.label: State of emergency declared
evidence: At least 169 people are dead and a state of emergency has been declared after Colombia was hit by one of its largest earthquakes in years.

nary_nodes.label: Injuries from earthquake
evidence: At least 900 people were injured in the quakes, Colombia's Association of Capital Cities (Asocapitales) wrote in an update on Tuesday.

nary_nodes.label: Building collapse in Pereira
evidence: Videos verified by the BBC show at least one building collapsing in Plaza Bolívar, Pereira's main square, with scattered debris and dust across the open space where many people had gathered.

nary_nodes.label: Damage to regional airports
evidence: The country's aviation authority has reported damage at several regional airports, including those in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura.

nary_nodes.label: Shaking in Bogotá
evidence: In the capital, Bogotá, trees and traffic lights shook violently, with reports of cracks in buildings but so far none of any serious damage to the city's infrastructure.

nary_nodes.label: Tremors felt in neighboring countries
evidence: Tremors were felt as far away as neighbouring Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama.

nary_nodes.label: Twin quakes in Venezuela
evidence: The quake comes less than two months after twin quakes devastated the north of Venezuela, killing more than 6,300 people.

nary_nodes.label: National disaster declared
evidence: Colombia's President Abelardo de la Espriella has declared a national disaster situation, creating special powers to react to the emergency, including to reallocate budgets.

nary_nodes.label: World leaders offer support
evidence: As the extent of the damage has begun to emerge, world leaders have come forward to offer support.

nary_nodes.label: Geological service reports quake details
evidence: The magnitude 7.4 quake struck at 07:34 (12:34 GMT) at a depth of 103km (64 miles) in Chocó province, the country's geological service said.

nary_nodes.label: Asocapitales reports injuries
evidence: At least 900 people were injured in the quakes, Colombia's Association of Capital Cities (Asocapitales) wrote in an update on Tuesday.

nary_nodes.label: Mayor Moncada reports no deaths in San José del Palmar
evidence: The epicentre of the quake was near the village of San José del Palmar, in Chocó province, but local mayor León Fabio Marín Moncada said that there had miraculously been no deaths or injuries - despite the roads in and out being damaged.

nary_nodes.label: Asocapitales reports most fatalities in cities
evidence: According to Asocapitales, most of the fatalities where in cities.

nary_nodes.label: Dan Cutler describes earthquake experience
evidence: Being woken by the earthquake, he told the BBC: "I've never experienced anything like it."
"We sprinted outside in our pyjamas. There's no major structural damage to the hotel, but there are surface cracks in the walls, and paint and plaster have peeled off," he says.

nary_nodes.label: Angélica Ávila describes earthquake experience
evidence: Speaking to BBC World Service, Angélica Ávila said she had been staying in a hotel in Manizales.
She said as the earthquake hit, cracks appeared in the walls.
"Everyone was screaming... I saw dust coming out of the neighbouring buildings, and bricks were falling off the walls," she said.

nary_nodes.label: Luis Felipe Molina explains building resistance
evidence: Journalist and meteorologist Luis Felipe Molina, from Manizales, was at home when the earthquake struck - about 150km from the epicentre.
He explained that due to previous earthquakes, the city has "very strict seismic-resistant building regulations" - so his building was able to resist the impact.
"I have 450 books and only a few were left standing on the shelves. You could hear glass breaking and people screaming," he told BBC Mundo.

nary_nodes.label: Aviation authority reports airport damage
evidence: The country's aviation authority has reported damage at several regional airports, including those in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura.

nary_nodes.label: Pope Leo XIV saddened by earthquake
evidence: A spokesman for Pope Leo XIV said the pontiff was "deeply saddened to learn the painful news of the earthquake".

nary_nodes.label: Marco Rubio monitors earthquake, offers support
evidence: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US was "closely monitoring" the earthquake, and stood "ready to support"

nary_nodes.label: Ursula von der Leyen reports Copernicus satellite use
evidence: EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said the EU's Copernicus satellite was being used in the rescue operation.

nary_nodes.label: Nayib Bukele sends solidarity, offers aid
evidence: The president of El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, sent a message of solidarity to the Colombian people and offered personnel and equipment for rescue efforts.

nary_nodes.label: US Geological Survey reports felt shaking
evidence: According to the US Geological Survey, an estimated 1.5 million people felt shaking close to magnitude seven.

But they can release energy in a way which is damaging to buildings, with fewer but potentially stronger aftershocks.
